title: Regular-module and scalar normalization for completed constant realization
statement: Let X be a scheme, A a commutative ring in the coefficient universe, and d an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let G be completed constant realization [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion], F the composite of restriction through the inverse canonical completed-ring isomorphism with the canonical small-site module equivalence, and O the completed coefficient ring on that site [def-weil-pbc-completed-cech-site-transport]. Set Q=G followed by F. The canonical map c from the regular O-module to Q(A), obtained by composing completedCechCoefficientUnit with F(completedKoszulOne), is an isomorphism. For every a in A, c followed by Q of multiplication by a equals multiplication by completedCechScalar(X,d,a) on O followed by c [def-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-system]. This assertion concerns modules and scalar maps only, with no complexes, transitions, or chosen exterior bases.

proof.text: Compose the scalar-extension/restriction Hom equivalence with constant-module sheafification and the regular-presheaf/global-sections equivalence. The normalized ordinary adjunction unit sends the constant generator 1 to 1 tensor 1. Thus this composite is precomposition with completedKoszulOne followed by the regular-sheaf/global-sections equivalence. Precomposition is bijective for every target module, so the Yoneda criterion proves completedKoszulOne invertible. Naturality of that unit for multiplication by a, and linearity of the module sheafification unit, show that the image of multiplication by a sends the distinguished section to the scalar section a times that section.

The transported unit is classified by section 1. Its linearity gives the explicit formula r maps to the inverse completed coefficient-ring isomorphism applied to r. The forward ring isomorphism is its sectionwise inverse, compatible with restrictions. Reindexing these maps proves completedCechCoefficientUnit invertible. Its composite with the transported completedKoszulOne is invertible. Test the desired scalar equality at section 1, use the scalar formula before transport, and cancel the inverse/forward coefficient-ring maps. The resulting scalar section is completedCechScalar by definition. These identities also hold for the zero ring and empty site.

lean.statement:
theorem completedRealizationRegular
    (X : Scheme.{u}) {A : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A) :
    let F := intrinsicPresentationModulesBack X d ⋙ (completedCechModulesEquiv X d).functor
    let G := completedKoszulConstant X (intrinsicPresentationDatum d)
    let Q := G ⋙ F
    let O := completedCechRing X d
    let c := completedCechCoefficientUnit X d ≫
      F.map (completedKoszulOne X (intrinsicPresentationDatum d))
    IsIso c ∧ ∀ a : A, c ≫ Q.map (ModuleCat.ofHom (LinearMap.mul A A a)) =
      ringedKoszulScalar O (completedCechScalar X d a) ≫ c
